## Purpose

In this assignment, you will compare the use of human-powered transport and public transit by calculating a paired samples t-test (sometimes called a dependent samples t-test) and a confidence interval for the difference of the means, and then you will interpret your findings. To learn more about the climate change impacts of transportation choices, see the links below.

[Health Benefits of Public Transport](https://transloc.com/blog/6-health-benefits-of-public-transportation/)

[Community Benefits of Public Transport](https://www.remix.com/blog/8-benefits-of-public-transportation)

## Comparing the Use of Human-Powered Transport and Public Transit

When they completed the Climate Change Action Inventory (Barchard, Okagawa, Hoffman, & Odents, 2021), participants were asked how frequently they use human-powered transport and how often they used public transit. The possible response options were: 

1 = Less than once a year 

2 = Once a year  

3 = Several times a year 

4 = Once a month  

5 = A couple times a month 

6 = Once a week  

7 = At least 3 times a week 

8 = At least 7 times a week  

9 = At least 14 times a week

You will conduct a paired samples t-test to test the null hypothesis that the mean difference in the frequency of human-powered transit and public transit is 0 ($𝐻_0: \mu_𝐷 = 0$) vs the alternative that the mean difference is not zero ($𝐻_1: \mu_D \ne 0$). 

1. Calculate a paired samples t-test for human-powered transport (**CCAI_Transportation4**) and public transit (**CCAI_Transportation5**). *Put the first variable in the left-hand side of the Paired Variables window, and the second in the right*. 

2. Request the Student’s t test.

3. Under Additional Statistics, ask for Descriptives and the 95% confidence interval for the Mean Difference.

4.  Use your results to answer the questions below.


::: {.callout-tip}

## Question 1
Across all participants, the mean frequency of using human-powered transport is `r forms_num((4.21), width = 6)` and the median is `r forms_num((4.00), width = 6)`. This translates to approximately `r forms_schoice(c("Once a year", "Once a month", "Once a week", "Several times a week"), c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE), display = "dropdown")`. 
:::

::: {.callout-tip}

## Question 2
On average, which do participants use more - human-powered or public transport?

`r forms_schoice(c("Public transport", "Human-powered transport"), c(FALSE, TRUE), display = "dropdown")`

:::

::: {.callout-tip}

## Question 3
The t-value is `r forms_num((13.47), width = 6)`, with `r forms_num((499), width = 6)` degrees of freedom. 

:::


::: {.callout-tip}

## Question 4
The p-value is `r forms_string("<.001")`, which should cause us to `r forms_schoice(c("reject", "retain"), c(TRUE, FALSE), display = "dropdown")` the null hypothesis. 

:::


::: {.callout-tip}

## Question 5

The lower limit of the confidence interval for the difference in the means is `r forms_num((1.38), width = 6)`, and the upper limit is `r forms_num((1.85), width = 6)`.

:::

## Question 6

Fill in the missing words and numbers (2dp for numbers, 3dp for p-values, 0 dp for degrees of freedom) - use the words from the scale above for interpretation of the numbers. 

Female participants' rating on how much they used human-powered transport on average was `r forms_num((3.75), width = 6)`, approximately `r forms_schoice(c("Once a year", "Once a month", "Once a week", "Several times a year"), c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE), display = "dropdown")`, and their rating on how much they used public transit on average was `r forms_num((3.75), width = 6)`, approximately `r forms_schoice(c("Once a year", "Once a month", "Once a week", "Several times a year"), c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE), display = "dropdown")`, *t*(`r forms_num((211), width = 6)` = `r forms_num((6.85), width = 6)`, *p* `r forms_string("<.001")`; 95% confidence interval for the mean difference = [`r forms_num((0.89), width = 6)`, `r forms_num((1.60), width = 6)`]).

:::
